sentences.text: If you pull a box up on a rope over a wheel, you have an elevator.
But a full car weighs about a thousand kilograms, and the motor alone has to lift all of it.
So the motor stalls, and the car sinks back down to the floor.
So you hang a counterweight on the other end of the rope, and the motor lifts only the difference.
The motor turns a grooved wheel, the ropes grip it, and the car rises as the counterweight sinks.
The counterweight usually weighs as much as the car plus about forty percent of a full load, so the two nearly balance.
But the light car and the counterweight now swing loose in the shaft.
So you bolt steel rails up the shaft, and the car rides on the rails and stops swinging.
But if a rope snaps, nothing stops the car from falling.
So you add a safety clamp that grips the rails, the trick Elisha Otis showed in 1854.
And one rope is not all that holds you up.
A real car hangs from four to eight steel ropes, and a single rope may be strong enough to hold the car alone.
Add sliding doors, a button panel and a ceiling light, and the car glides down to the floor.
Congratulations, you have built an elevator.
